page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.large is an entry-level compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at a clock frequency of 3.3 GHz across 2 vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 execution threads. The x86_64 processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory consists of 4.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

A key physical attribute of the c5ad.large instance is its storage subsystem, which features a bundled 75 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. This local storage delivers lower latency and higher input/output throughput than standard remote EBS volumes, though it acts as ephemeral storage. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline throughput of 1 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned by default.

In synthetic benchmarks, the server demonstrates moderate single-threaded capability alongside constrained multi-core throughput due to its single physical core design. The AMD EPYC core achieves an average Geekbench single-core score of 1321.0, single-threaded gzip compression at 24.93 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression at 9.55 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-heavy workloads fall into lower performance tiers, characterized by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1666.0, PassMark CPU score of 2867.98, and static web serving throughput of 2.23 GB/sec.

Given its compute-oriented core-to-RAM ratio paired with rapid local NVMe storage, the c5ad.large delivers practical cost efficiency for budget-conscious compute tasks that do not require wide parallel scaling. The instance is suited for lightweight build agents, batch processing tasks, caching layers, log processing, and continuous integration pipelines needing fast ephemeral scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services c5ad.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor clocked at 3.3 GHz, it provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core, complemented by 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory. The instance includes a built-in 75 GB NVMe SSD for fast local scratch storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps without hardware accelerators. Synthetic benchmarks reflect solid single-thread performance, posting 1321.0 in Geekbench single-core and 24.93 GB/sec in gzip compression, while multi-threaded capacity remains bounded by its two-thread limit. With its 2:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and high-speed instance storage, c5ad.large provides a resource-dense, cost-effective profile for intermediate build runners, lightweight batch operations, log parsing, and development workloads requiring low-latency ephemeral disk access.
